title: Color Leaves for Diverse Nodes
statement:
You are given an unweighted, undirected tree with `n` nodes numbered `0` to `n - 1`. The tree is **rooted at node `0`**. A **leaf** is a node that has no children (so when `n = 1`, the root itself is the only leaf). The subtree of a node `x` is `x` together with all of its descendants.

You must color every leaf with a color of your choice (colors are just labels; use as many or as few as you like). Internal nodes are not colored. A node `x` is called **diverse** if all the leaves in the subtree of `x` have pairwise different colors. A leaf is always diverse, because its subtree contains only itself.

For every `i` from `1` to `n`, determine the **minimum number of different colors** that a coloring of the leaves must use so that **at least `i` nodes** of the tree are diverse. It is always possible to reach `n` diverse nodes (give every leaf its own color), so every answer exists.

Return an array of `n` integers where the `i`-th value (1-indexed) is that minimum.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n - 1` lines contains two integers `u` and `v`, an edge between nodes `u` and `v` (0-indexed). The tree is rooted at node `0`.
outputFormat: Print `n` space-separated integers: the answers for `i = 1, 2, ..., n`.
constraints: The input is a tree (connected, n - 1 edges), rooted at node 0
The depth of the tree (number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path) is at most 5000

examples.explanation: Leaves are 2, 3 and 4. Subtree leaf counts: node 0 has 3, node 1 has 2, and nodes 2, 3, 4 have 1 each. With one color the three leaves are diverse, so i = 1, 2, 3 cost 1. Node 1 is diverse only if its leaves 3 and 4 differ (2 colors), giving 4 diverse nodes. The root is diverse only if all three leaves differ (3 colors), giving 5.
The tree is a path. Node 3 is the only leaf, so every subtree contains at most one leaf and all four nodes are diverse with a single color.
The root is the only leaf, and it is diverse using one color.

hints: A node can only be diverse if its subtree has at most c leaves when you use c colors. Count the leaves in every subtree first (children before parents).

With c colors, can you make every node whose subtree has at most c leaves diverse at the same time? Think about the order in which a DFS visits leaves: the leaves of any subtree are consecutive in that order.
Color the leaves cyclically 0, 1, ..., c-1 in DFS order. Then the answer for i is just the i-th smallest subtree leaf count.
